Antecedentes Clínicos:
Artrosis.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Rotura horizontal oblicuo del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial con segmento
parcialmente desplazado al receso menisco tibial a nivel del cuerpo.
Rotura horizontal del cuerno anterior, cuerpo y parte del cuerno posterior del menisco lateral, sin
desplazamiento de segmentos.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la región central y de carga del compartimento
femorotibial medial. Cartílagos del compartimento femorotibial lateral sin alteraciones.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la articulación patelofemoral.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Rotura del menisco medial con segmento parcialmente desplazado receso menisco tibial.
Rotura del menisco lateral, no desplazada.
Condropatía con lesiones grado 2 del compartimento femorotibial medial y patelofemoral

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Three-month history knee pain after fall. Anterior knee pain. No prior surgery.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Small focal incomplete complex tear of the posterior root lateral meniscus. No meniscal extrusion or displaced fragment.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. Patella alta. Shallow trochlear sulcus. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Focal soft tissue edema about the anterolateral knee interposed between the lateral femoral condyle and distal iliotibial band. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Small focal incomplete complex tear at the posterior root lateral meniscus without extrusion or displaced fragment.
2.	Findings compatible with distal iliotibial band friction syndrome.

- In the medial compartment, there is horizontal tear from anterior to posterior horn. Complex tear with gap 5 mm at posterior horn. 
 There is diffuse high grade chondrosis (more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along weight-baring medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau. There is subchondral edema. Subchondral bone cyst is present. Osteophytes are present.  
 - The lateral compartment, contusional injury at anterior horn of meniscus.  
  
 - The patellofemoral joint, there is diffuse low grade chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along medial, lateral patellar facets, medial and lateral trochleas. There is no subchondral edema. Osteophytes are present. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
  
 - In the intercondylar notch,  
 ACL high grade partial tear.  
 the posterior cruciate ligaments are intact.  
  
 - MCL;  
 superficial; intact 
 deep; high grade injury 
 - LCL; high grade injury at femoral attachment 
 - Popliteus tendon; low grade injury at femoral attachment 
  
  
 - The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Some amount of left knee effusion with synovitis is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion. - LCL; high grade injury at femoral attachment 
 - ACL high grade partial tear.  
 -- Some amount of left knee effusion with synovitis 
 - Medial meniscus;  horizontal tear from anterior to posterior horn. Complex tear with gap 5 mm at posterior horn. 
 - Lateral meniscus; contusional injury at anterior horn of meniscus.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain for 2 months after fall. 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Small heterogenous T2 hyperintense lesion at the medial femoral metaphysis, consistent with a nonaggressive chondroid lesion.

JOINT SPACE:
Large joint effusion with synovial proliferation. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Markedly diminutive, related to prior debridement, with extensive complex tearing of the remnant meniscus and maceration of the body.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage denudation in the weightbearing compartment with broad areas of full-thickness cartilage loss, large marginal osteophytes and subchondral marrow edema.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Inner margin tearing of the body and anterior horn. No extrusion. 
Lateral compartment cartilage: High-grade chondrosis with superimposed full-thickness fissuring at the weightbearing lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau with large marginal spurs.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade chondrosis with superimposed full-thickness fissuring, most prominent at the lateral patellar facet and lateral trochlea, and large marginal spurs.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Chronic high-grade ACL tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact. Bowing with reactive periligamentous edema, related to meniscal pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with associated enthesopathy. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 12 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. Multilobulated ganglion cyst extending into the popliteus sheath. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritis, most advanced in the medial compartment.
2.	Markedly diminutive medial meniscus, related to prior debridement, with extensive complex tearing of the remnant meniscus and maceration of the body.
3.	Chronic high-grade tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL).
4.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with associated enthesopathy.
5.	Moderate right knee effusion.

Constatations :

Il n’y a pas d’épanchement intra-articulaire significatif au genou.

Il n’y a pas de kyste poplité. Minime liséré de liquide dans la bourse semi-membraneuse.

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts. Il y a une structure ovoïde liquidienne de 0.6 x 0.4 x 0.3cm entre les ligaments croisés qui pourrait refléter une petite loculation du liquide intra-articulaire VS un petit kyste ganglionnaire (image 19, série 3).

Compartiment antérieur :

Il y a des fissure de cartilage de grade modéré à haut à la facette médiale et à la crête médiane de la rotule. Il y a aussi des changements de signal au cartilage de la facette latérale de la rotule suggérant une chondropathie débutante. Il y a des fissure de grade modéré à l’aspect inférieur de la trochlée particulièrement à son aspect central et médial. Minime quantité de liquide dans la bourse infra-patellaire profonde.

Compartiment interne :

Léger amincissement de cartilage diffus. Le ménisque interne et le ligament collatéral interne sont sans particularité.

Compartiment externe :

Légère chondropathie. Il y a des changements de signal hyperintense T2 intrasubstance à la corne antérieure/racine antérieure du ménisque latéral suggérant des changements dégénératifs. Le complexe ligamentaire latéral est sans particularité.

Conclusion :

Chondropathie modérée au compartiment antérieur et légère au compartiment interne et externe.

Il n’y a pas de kyste poplité.

Il y a un probable kyste ganglionnaire de 6mm entre les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia izquierda.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Fibrilación marginal asociado a imagen sugerente de pequeña rotura del cuerpo del menisco lateral.
Rotura compleja del cuerpo, cuerno posterior y parte de la raíz meniscal posterior del menisco medial con
segmento laminar desplazado hacia la región intercondílea posterior. Importante extrusión meniscal, con
edema las partes blandas regionales.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial y total de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial medial con
mínimos cambios óseos secundarios periféricos del platillo tibial medial.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibial lateral y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones. Úlceras
condrales de espesor total con cambios óseos secundarios de la faceta medial y vértice de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular con sinovitis difusa.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de
límites normales.
Impresión:
Fibrilación marginal asociado a imagen sugerente de pequeña rotura del cuerpo del menisco lateral.
Extensa rotura compleja del cuerpo, cuerno posterior y parte de la raíz meniscal posterior del menisco
medial con segmento laminar desplazado hacia la región intercondílea posterior con extrusión meniscal y
edema las partes blandas regionales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 3 y 4 del compartimento femorotibial medial y de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular con sinovitis difusa

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Rotura del menisco medial.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones en significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Rotura marginal del cuerno posterior, cuerpo y parte del cuerno anterior del menisco lateral con
mínima extrusión meniscal.
Rotura compleja del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial con componente principal
horizontal oblicuo. Impresiona parcial desplazamiento de segmento al receso menisco tibial a la
altura del cuerpo con discreto edema las partes blandas adyacentes.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de la zona de carga de los compartimentos femorotibiales,
más evidentes en el cóndilo femoral lateral. No hay cambios óseos secundarios.
Cartílagos patelofemorales sin alteraciones significativas.
Leve derrame articular. No hay quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Rotura marginal del menisco lateral con mínima extrusión meniscal.
Rotura compleja del menisco medial con segmento parcialmente desplazado receso menisco tibial
a nivel del cuerpo.
Condropatía con lesiones grado 2 y 3 de los compartimentos femorotibiales.
Leve derrame articular.

Na seriji MR presjeka lijevog koljena nalazi se uredna morfologija i intenziteti signala kolateralnih
ligamenata, prednjeg i stražnjeg križnog ligamenta, iliotibijalnog traktusa, patelarnog ligamenta i
tetive m. kvadricepsa.
Kompleksna flap ruptura u području korpusa i stražnjeg roga medijlanog meniska, čija se flap
komponenta prebacuje uz gornji rub stražnjeg korijena meniska.
Lateralni menisk uredne je morfologije i intenziteta signala.
Subhondralna T2 hiperintenzivna linija u srednjem dijelu medijalnog kondila femura na arealu
14x4 mm, bez okolnog koštanog edema ili lezije pripadajuće zglobne hrskavice - opisano u
smislu stabilnog osteohondritis disekansa.
Plitke fisure hrskavice obje fasete patele te medijalnog kondila femura i tibije (hondromalacija 2.
stupnja prema ICRS klasifikaciji).
Fisure pune debljine hrskavice obje fasete patele (hondromalacija 2. stupnja prema ICRS
klasifikaciji).
Ostale prikazane artikulacijske hrskavice urednih su intenziteta signala.
Minimalan izljev u koljenu. Sitna poplitealna (Bakerova) cista.
Bipartitna patela tip 3 kao anatomska varijanta.
Ostale prikazane koštane, mekotkivne i neurovaskularne strukture uredne su morfologije i
intenziteta signala.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Osteoarthritis.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Bone marrow edema at the medial tibial plateau, likely reactive. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion, incompletely imaged, with synovial proliferation. Trace leaking Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn, with dominant complete radial tear at the posterior horn-root junction. Moderate meniscal body extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity with areas of full-thickness fissuring at the weightbearing aspect of the joint.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Degeneration without discrete tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the posterior lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse low-grade cartilage loss at the patella with areas of full-thickness fissuring at the lateral and medial facets. Focal high-grade cartilage loss of the central trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Mild mucoid degeneration.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema, likely related to adjacent meniscal pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis. Patellar enthesopathy. Mild patellar tendinosis.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. Patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 10 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Fluid tracking into the popliteus tendon sheath.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Complex tear of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with dominant complete radial component at the posterior horn-root junction. Moderate meniscal body extrusion.
2.	Bone marrow edema at the medial tibial plateau, concerning for early subchondral insufficiency fracture.
3.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, overall mild to moderate. Moderate knee joint effusion. Trace leaking Baker's cyst.
4.	Mild distal quadriceps and patellar tendinosis.
